title: Samsung Projects Record $80 B Q3 Profit Fueled by AI Boom, CNBC Reports
body:
Samsung Electronics announced on Thursday that its preliminary operating profit for the third quarter has surged to 107.4 trillion won (about $80 billion), marking the first time the South Korean conglomerate has broken the 100‑trillion‑won threshold in a single quarter. The unprecedented earnings boost is being credited largely to the company’s aggressive push into artificial‑intelligence (AI)‑enabled semiconductors and memory chips, which have seen soaring demand from data‑center operators, smartphone makers and emerging generative‑AI platforms.

The earnings outlook reflects a broader shift in the semiconductor industry, where AI workloads are driving a new wave of capital investment. Samsung’s latest wafer‑fab expansions in South Korea and the United States have been geared toward producing high‑bandwidth memory (HBM) and advanced logic chips that power AI accelerators. Analysts note that the firm’s “foundry‑plus‑memory” model—selling both the processing cores and the high‑speed memory that feed them—has positioned Samsung to capture a larger share of the AI supply chain than many of its rivals, which tend to specialize in one segment or the other.

Beyond AI, Samsung’s strong performance also stems from a rebound in its flagship smartphone division and continued dominance in the global DRAM and NAND flash markets. While the premium‑phone segment remains competitive, the company’s latest Galaxy models have benefited from integrated AI features that enhance camera performance, battery management and user personalization, driving higher average selling prices. Meanwhile, inventory levels in the memory business have stabilized after a period of oversupply, allowing Samsung to command better pricing as cloud providers and automotive OEMs ramp up AI‑centric projects.

The record profit forecast has implications for Samsung’s broader corporate strategy. Chief Executive Officer Han Jong‑hee reaffirmed the group’s commitment to “next‑generation” technologies, signalling further investment in 3‑nanometer process nodes and advanced packaging techniques such as chip‑on‑wafer‑module (CoWoS) and integrated fan‑out (InFO). The company also hinted at expanding its AI‑focused software ecosystem, aiming to provide end‑to‑end solutions that combine hardware, silicon‑level AI libraries and cloud services. Such vertical integration could deepen Samsung’s relationships with major AI developers and reduce reliance on third‑party software stacks.

Investors have responded positively, with Samsung’s shares rising sharply in after‑hours trading and the company’s market capitalization approaching the $500 billion mark. However, some market watchers caution that the AI‑driven surge may be tempered by macro‑economic headwinds, including slower consumer spending in key regions and potential geopolitical tensions that could disrupt supply chains. Additionally, competition from rivals such as Taiwan’s TSMC, which is also scaling its AI‑centric offerings, could compress margins if price wars intensify.

Looking ahead, Samsung’s ability to sustain this momentum will hinge on how quickly it can translate its AI‑centric product roadmap into commercial volume. The firm is slated to begin mass production of its next‑generation HBM and AI‑optimized processors later this year, with customers ranging from hyperscale data centers to automotive chipmakers. If demand continues to outpace supply, Samsung could see its operating profit climb even higher in the fourth quarter, reinforcing its status as the world’s most valuable semiconductor company. Conversely, any slowdown in AI spending or a resurgence of inventory excess could temper growth. For now, the historic profit milestone underscores Samsung’s successful bet on AI as a catalyst for the next era of semiconductor profitability.
